category: Digital-product fulfilment — largest per-file number in the group

free_tier.stated: Own help centre: 'If you price your product at any number greater than $0.99, the largest single file that you can upload to a product is 20 GB in size... you can add as many files as you want to each product.' Free/$0 products are capped at 250 MB cumulative.

per_object_cap.stated: largest single file that you can upload to a product is 20 GB

egress.terms: CloudFront in front of S3 (confirmed in their open-source repo: CLOUDFRONT_* + FILE_DOWNLOAD_DISTRIBUTION_URL_PROD). No per-download quota published.

interface_detail: Web + documented REST API (products, product_files); the codebase is open source (antiwork/gumroad), so limits are inspectable.
tooling: REST API with access token; the repo exposes /attachments/... presigned paths via SignedUrlHelper.
chaining: The $0.99 pricing gate is the mechanism: price at $1, get 20 GB/file, unlimited files per product, unlimited products. A $1 product that never sells still costs the seller ~nothing after fees. 20 GB x N files.

limits.value: largest single file that you can upload to a product is 20 GB

limits_note: per-object-cap 20 GB (products >$0.99) / 250 MB cumulative (priced $0). 'Download all' button only appears under 500 MB total content, but a single ZIP sidesteps that. Repo shows MAX_EPUB_READER_ARCHIVE_SIZE = 32 MB and thumbnail cap 5 MB — those are feature caps, not the product-file cap.
reliability_note: Purchases require a payment method on the seller side to withdraw, but uploading does not. Download URLs are presigned CloudFront/S3 and short-lived, so there is no stable hot-link — archive/delivery tier only.

evidence.proved: '20 GB File size limit' and '250 MB limit' sections, verbatim

raw.githubusercontent.com/antiwork/gumroad/main/app/models/product_file.rb — confirms S3/CloudFront storage classes and that 20 GB is not enforced in this model, i.e. it is a policy cap at the uploader
